top_choice_rationale: P001 (B048, Melitz and Helpman) is a mechanism-level discovery: selection of heterogeneous firms into exporting and reallocation across firms. It made predictions that could have failed (exporter premia, selection, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation), and these have largely held in firm-level data across many countries over more than twenty years. Melitz (2003) is the identifiable originating model, and Helpman's exporting-versus-FDI work with Melitz and Yeaple makes the two-name credit coherent. A citation limited to the selection-and-reallocation mechanism and the gains-from-trade channel avoids overclaiming the parallel empirical work of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum. That priority question and the dependence of welfare magnitudes on functional form remain real limits, but they do not outweigh the maturity and robustness of the core claims. I rank it above no award.
recusal_note: No tie to Melitz or Helpman is apparent from my profile. My profile records Harvard appointments (2006-17), the Harvard evolutionary-dynamics network, close co-authorship with former committee member Magnus Johannesson, and SSE ties to Tore Ellingsen and Johan Almenberg; none is a candidate connection. My metascience and replication work, including with the Institute for Replication, makes me weigh robustness more heavily than influence. This is disclosed, not adjudicated.
